questions.q: About whom was the declaration in chapter 23 spoken?
questions.a: The declaration in chapter 23 was about Tyre.

questions.q: Why should the ships of Tarshish wail?
questions.a: They should wail because they have neither home nor harbor.

questions.q: Who made the people of the coastland wealthy by trading across the sea?
questions.a: The merchants of Sidon made them wealthy by trading across the sea.

questions.q: What was the city of Tyre?
questions.a: Tyre was the marketplace of the nations.

questions.q: What does the sea say about Tyre?
questions.a: The sea says it has no people left, as if it never had children or raised young men and women.

questions.q: What will the Egyptians do when they hear the report about Tyre?
questions.a: The Egyptians will tremble with grief.

questions.q: What should the ships and people of the coastland do?
questions.a: They should cross over toward Tarshish and weep with grief.

questions.q: What did the people of Tyre do in other lands long ago?
questions.a: They went out and settled in many other lands.

questions.q: Who planned this against Tyre?
questions.a: Yahweh of Armies planned this against Tyre.

questions.q: Why has Yahweh planned this against Tyre?
questions.a: He has planned this to dishonor her pride and all her glory, to make light of all her honored ones of the earth.

questions.q: What should the people who lived by the sea now do?
questions.a: They should spread out over the land and farm it, since they no longer need to live by the sea.

questions.q: What did Yahweh command concerning Tyre, the merchant city?
questions.a: Yahweh commanded that its strongholds be destroyed.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say would happen if the people of Tyre fled to Cyprus?
questions.a: He said they would not have a peaceful life there either.

questions.q: What did the Assyrians do to the land of the Chaldeans?
questions.a: They turned it into a place for desert animals and destroyed its towers and palaces.

questions.q: What has happened to the stronghold of the ships of Tarshish?
questions.a: It has been destroyed.

questions.q: How long will Tyre be forgotten?
questions.a: Tyre will be forgotten for 70 years.

questions.q: What is the forgotten prostitute told to do so people will remember her?
questions.a: She is told to take a harp, walk through the city, and sing many songs.

questions.q: What will happen to Tyre after being forgotten for 70 years?
questions.a: Yahweh will restore Tyre, and she will return to earning money by trading with all the kingdoms of the earth.

questions.q: What will happen to Tyre’s profits and earnings?
questions.a: They will be dedicated to Yahweh.

questions.q: What will happen to Tyre’s merchandise?
questions.a: It will be for those who worship Yahweh, so they can have the food and clothing they need.

commentary.text: The overthrow of Tyre. (Is. 23:1-14) It is established again. (Is. 23:15-18)

Is. 23:1-14 Tyre was the mart of the nations. She was noted for mirth and diversions; and this made her loth to consider the warnings God gave by his servants. Her merchants were princes, and lived like princes. Tyre being destroyed and laid waste, the merchants should abandon her. Flee to shift for thine own safety; but those that are uneasy in one place, will be so in another; for when God's judgments pursue sinners, they will overtake them. Whence shall all this trouble come? It is a destruction from the Almighty. God designed to convince men of the vanity and uncertainty of all earthly glory. Let the ruin of Tyre warn all places and persons to take heed of pride; for he who exalts himself shall be abased. God will do it, who has all power in his hand; but the Chaldeans shall be the instruments.

Is. 23:15-18 The desolations of Tyre were not to be for ever. The Lord will visit Tyre in mercy. But when set at liberty, she will use her old arts of temptation. The love of worldly wealth is spiritual idolatry; and covetousness is spiritual idolatry. This directs those that have wealth, to use it in the service of God. When we abide with God in our worldly callings, when we do all in our power to further the gospel, then our merchandise and hire are holiness to the Lord, if we look to his glory. Christians should carry on business as God's servants, and use riches as his stewards.
